correctness.rationale: The cyclic-rotation orbits of two-marker supports are indexed by shorter separation d. Their periods are n for d<n/2 and n/2 for antipodal d=n/2. In a single orbit, rotations by one or two correspond to forbidden overlap lengths n−1,n−2, so any chosen phases must have cyclic distance≥3, giving floor(P_d/3). The construction selects phases r=3j in each orbit; its proof splits shifted-prefix/suffix tests by whether zero, one, or two support markers are dropped and rules out cross-orbit violations, including even antipodal ties and self-pairs. Independent direct pairwise checking confirmed constructed code sizes and both overlap constraints for every n=4..50. This supports the all-n orbit argument but cannot prove it by enumeration.

limitations: Exactly two ones, n>=4, and only the two longest proper overlaps; code uses all directed pair constraints including identical words.
